divergences: E8.4 applicability (#1079): my agent definition gates sub-elements 3 AND 4 jointly on a referenced code repository or software-production-as-output. The launch message makes sub-element 4 applicable to every dataset that was processed at all, gating only sub-element 3 on the repository clause. No outcome difference here: external_resources references github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, so both readings reach applicable for both sub-elements.

E8.4 threshold (#1059): my definition says a pointer identifying only the publisher (an organisation root, a project homepage) scores 0. The launch message says such a pointer neither earns nor forfeits the point, and adds a case (c) absent from my definition: a named pipeline whose outputs the record says are not in this release leaves what produced the release unstated. I applied the launch message text, including case (c), which materially shaped the E8.4 reasoning for this record.
E4 (#1060): my definition already carries per-sub-element applicability with the governance disjunct on sub-elements 1-2 only. Matches the launch message.

issues_detected.description: Every preprocessing, cleaning and labeling entry describes the MuSIC / Cell Mapping Toolkit pipeline, and each carries a source caveat stating that the computed cell maps that pipeline produces are not included in this release. The record therefore documents a pipeline in detail while leaving unstated what software processed the artifacts actually distributed: the mass spectrometry search and quantification for the AP-MS and SEC-MS archives, and the alignment and demultiplexing for the perturb-seq archives.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a software_and_tools block naming the per-modality processing software with versions (mass spectrometry search engine, single-cell alignment pipeline, image acquisition and processing software), distinguishing it from the downstream MuSIC pipeline.

issues_detected.description: The record omits publisher, and source_caveats states the omission is deliberate because the bundle names no publisher for the release. The citation the record itself supplies ends 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2', and page, maintainers, retention_limit and data_governance all identify that repository. The platform is unambiguous everywhere except the slot designated for it.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) as publisher; the record's own citation already asserts it.

issues_detected.description: Top-level version is 2.0 and version_access marks it current, while two superseded releases are listed at Version 2.1 and the citation renders this release as V2. A prior release carrying a higher internal version number than the current one is explainable by Dataverse per-dataset version histories, but the record does not say so at the point where the numbers collide.
issues_detected.recommendation: Note in version_details that each quarterly release is a separate Dataverse dataset with an independent internal version counter, so version numbers are not comparable across releases.

issues_detected.description: No errata or change-log field records what changed in this release relative to the October 2025 release. The substantive change evidence the record does hold sits in source_caveats as the generator's own observation, that the three immunofluorescence archives report identical file sizes but different MD5 checksums and were therefore regenerated, and that AP-MS archives are newly present while perturb-seq external links moved from Sequence Read Archive links to embargoed.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add an errata or release-notes entry stating what changed at release scope: AP-MS archives added, immunofluorescence archives regenerated, perturb-seq external links embargoed.

issues_detected.description: The two cell-line identifiers use the Cellosaurus RRID namespace, RRID:CVCL_0419 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3, rather than the SCR_ or AB_ namespaces this rubric names. Both are well-formed registered RRIDs and correct for cell lines; the rubric's enumerated prefixes are incomplete, not the record.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change required to the record.

semantic_insights: The DOI prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse prefix, matching the landing page, the citation and the deposit narrative throughout the record. Format and registrar are both plausible.

The record correctly resolves a real source conflict rather than averaging it: the project portal states 'Released on: June 17, 2025' for the June 2026 release while Dataverse gives 2026-06-17, and the record prefers the higher-ranked Dataverse record and says so.

Deidentification reasoning is semantically appropriate for the data type. No identifier removal is claimed; the basis is that the material is commercially available cell lines that cannot be matched to a human subject with current knowledge. Claiming HIPAA Safe Harbor here would have been the semantic error.

The record declines to assert a protein count for the image archives, having noticed that the June 2026 archives report the same file sizes as the October 2025 ones but different MD5 checksums. That is a substantive evidence judgement, not a gap.

Grant identifiers follow NIH conventions: 1OT2OD032742-01 and core project OT2OD032742 (OT2 activity code, OD institute), plus 5U54HG012513-02 for the Bridge2AI Bridge Center. All parse correctly for the stated agency.
total_file_count of 10 reconciles exactly against the per-collection file counts in file_collections, 3 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1.

Temporal ordering is coherent: creation 2025-02-27, publication 2026-06-17 for seven archives, 2026-07-15 for the three immunofluorescence archives, against an NIH project period of 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31.
confidentiality_level of unrestricted is not in tension with the non-commercial license. Access requires no request; use is licensed. The record keeps those two axes separate correctly.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?
elements.applicability_note: Applicability resolved per sub-element, not as a block (#1060). Human-subjects condition FAILS on external evidence: the description names two cell lines and their derivatives rather than participants or patients; the 30 keywords are assay, cell-line and program terms with no clinical, patient or participant term; and collection_mechanisms (E8) describes endogenous tagging, chromatography, robotic staining and CRISPR screens, with no recruitment. Governance condition PASSES on E2 evidence: regulatory_restrictions states that use in clinical decision-making or patient care requires regulatory oversight and approval, other_compliance names a Data Governance Committee contact, and ip_restrictions routes commercial use through a Data Access Committee. That is a constraint that applies, not a record that none applies. Sub-elements 1-2 therefore open on the governance disjunct and are scored; sub-elements 3-5 open only on the human-subjects condition and are excluded.

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Governance condition met on E2 fields: regulatory_restrictions requires regulatory oversight for clinical use, other_compliance names the Data Governance Committee contact Jillian Parker, ip_restrictions names a Data Access Committee supervising ethical matters and dual licensing. Human-subjects condition not met, but this sub-element carries the governance disjunct.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews with reviewing_organization: CM4AI Ethics module and contact_person ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801; human_subject_research.ethics_review_board explaining that oversight runs through the Ethics module with named review contacts and that no IRB approval is recorded because no human subjects are involved.
sub_elements.quality_note: Oversight is documented as a structure rather than as a missing IRB number, and the absence of IRB approval is explained rather than left blank. The Ethics module's methodology is described concretely: Value-Sensitive Design, an axiological repository of values, a CM4AI Life Cycle framework of governance milestones.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?
elements.applicability_note: Collection identified and datasets shared, so sub-elements 1, 2 and 5 are applicable. Sub-element 3 is applicable on its own gate: external_resources references the code repository github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline. Sub-element 4 is applicable under #1079 as quoted in the launch message, because the dataset was processed at all, established from the collection and preprocessing fields; it would also be applicable under the repository clause.

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: collection_mechanisms and acquisition_methods populated; datasets shared via the Dataverse release.
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: four entries naming endogenous tagging of 17 genes in MDA-MB-468 with 34 more in progress, SEC-MS across three conditions and four iPSC states, robotic fixation and permeabilization with Human Protein Atlas antibodies and four-channel confocal readout, and CRISPR lentiviral screens with 6 guide RNAs per gene in inducible dCas9 lines read out on the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit; collection_timeframes and data_collectors also populated.
sub_elements.quality_note: Protocol-level detail sufficient for a domain reader to understand how each modality was produced, with the performing laboratory named per modality in data_collectors.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: four entries for AP-MS on endogenously tagged lines, SEC-MS as an orthogonal approach, ICC-IF with Human Protein Atlas antibodies followed by confocal microscopy, and single-cell CRISPRi screens, each with was_directly_observed true and was_reported_by_subjects false; raw_data_sources naming ATCC, HipSci and the MassIVE deposits.
sub_elements.quality_note: Instruments, reagent resources and observation flags are all recorded, and the raw sources upstream of each archive are traceable to their repositories.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: external_resources (E10 field) references a code repository: 'Cell Mapping Toolkit, an end-to-end Python pipeline for cell map construction: https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline'.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: four MuSIC pipeline steps (node2vec dimensionality reduction of protein-protein interaction networks, Human Protein Atlas deep learning image embedding, contrastive co-embedding, community detection); cleaning_strategies: FAIRSCAPE client validation and RO-Crate packaging per pipeline segment, plus quality control before release; labeling_strategies: alignment to Gene Ontology and Reactome plus large language model naming with confidence scores.
sub_elements.quality_note: All four named field families are populated with specific, non-boilerplate methods. Each MuSIC step carries an honest caveat that the computed cell maps are not in this release, which is an accuracy strength; the residual gap is that per-modality processing of the distributed archives is not described.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: `third_party_sharing: - is_shared: true`, 'The release is publicly downloadable from the University of Virginia Dataverse under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0', with `distribution_formats` 'ZIP archives containing RO-Crate packaged data files and metadata'. Processed at all: `preprocessing_strategies` (four entries), `cleaning_strategies` (two entries, including 'Data generated by the acquisition modules undergo quality control before release') and `labeling_strategies` are all populated.
sub_elements.evidence: `preprocessing_strategies` names 'the node2vec deep learning model' and 'a Human Protein Atlas deep learning model'; `cleaning_strategies` names 'the FAIRSCAPE client package to validate inputs and to create the output RO-Crate package for that segment'; `external_resources` names 'Cell Mapping Toolkit, an end-to-end Python pipeline for cell map construction: https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline', 'FAIRSCAPE AI-readiness framework' and 'Integrative Modeling Platform (IMP) package'. This record carries no `machine_annotation_tools` slot, so DenseNet-121, GPT-4 and HiDeF are not named here by name.
sub_elements.quality_note: This record makes the exclusion explicit at each entry rather than leaving it to be read across the document: every `preprocessing_strategies` entry carries a `source_caveats` of the form 'a step of the MuSIC pipeline that produces cell maps; the June 2026 release states that computed cell maps are not included in this release', and the first adds '... so this step was not applied to the artifacts distributed here'; the `labeling_strategies` caveat says the same. That is role (e) stated by the record itself. The FAIRSCAPE cleaning entry is role (d) for the input validation and role (c) for the RO-Crate package - its own caveat says 'the release itself is distributed with RO-Crate metadata and provenance produced by the same FAIRSCAPE framework', i.e. metadata production, not transformation of the data inside. The second cleaning entry ('quality control before release') names no software. Same verdict as rep1 and rep2; the difference between the records is bookkeeping - rep3 attaches the exclusion to each entry and omits `machine_annotation_tools` - not a difference in what software is disclosed as having produced the released artifacts.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared via the public Dataverse release.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: two preprints with DOIs (10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and 10.1101/2024.11.03.621734, the latter with PMCID PMC11580897), MassIVE and Figshare deposits, the CM4AI portal and data-releases page, and four tool and documentation sites; conforms_to naming RO-Crate, ARK, the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology and JSON-Schema.
sub_elements.quality_note: Publications, repositories, standards and documentation are each represented, with archival status flagged per group.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: five typed entries covering scope (no computed cell maps in this interim release), coverage (incompletely overlapping protein panels; imaging limited to MDA-MB-468), temporal (pre-publication embargo on perturb-seq links) and methodological (domain expertise required), three with recommended mitigation or scope impact.
sub_elements.quality_note: Limitation types are drawn from a controlled vocabulary and each carries a consequence for the reuser, such as analyses requiring all three modalities being limited to the panel intersection.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: representation_bias, with affected_subsets naming both donor-derived lines and their donor characteristics, and selection_bias over targeted protein panels with a mitigation_strategy citing the expansion to a genome-scale screen of 11,739 genes; future_use_impacts: three entries on generalization limits, the Ethics module's anticipation of downstream applications, and clinical misuse.
sub_elements.quality_note: Bias types use the enumerated taxonomy, affected subsets are named, and one bias carries a real mitigation rather than an acknowledgement. Downstream social impact is addressed through the Ethics module's governance framework.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: No anomalies slot. The only quality-process statement is in cleaning_strategies, that single-cell CRISPR screen data were being quality controlled at the time of the preprint.
sub_elements.quality_note: No documentation of outliers, batch effects, failed acquisitions or QC exclusions. The missing-data and coverage content that does exist is scored under Element 5 and Element 9 sub-element 1; nothing addresses anomalies within the released data.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present false with sensitivity_details explaining that the released content is laboratory measurements on commercially available cell lines rather than personal identifiers or protected health information.
sub_elements.quality_note: An explicit reasoned negative determination rather than an empty field, and the reasoning is tied to what the archives actually contain.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: reviewing_organization CM4AI Ethics module, contact_person ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801, review_details describing Value-Sensitive Design methodology, an axiological repository of values, a CM4AI Life Cycle governance framework and mixed empirical research; data_governance.stewardship_roles naming ethical review contacts with addresses.
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethical review is documented as a named body with named contacts and a described methodology. Conflicts of interest are not addressed anywhere in the record, which is the partial gap within an otherwise substantive field.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets shared condition met, so sub-elements 1, 3, 4 and 5 are applicable. Sub-element 2 additionally requires a publication identified elsewhere: external_resources names two preprints with DOIs and citation is populated, so it is applicable.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Public Dataverse release with distribution_formats and access URLs populated.
sub_elements.evidence: page resolves to dataverse.lib.virginia.edu; citation ends 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; maintainers name 'University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), School of Medicine collection'; retention_limit and data_governance both name the same repository; third_party_sharing adds MassIVE and Figshare.
sub_elements.quality_note: The publishing platform is unambiguous and stated in five places. The designated publisher slot is empty, deliberately, on the stated ground that the bundle names no publisher for the release, which sits oddly beside the record's own citation naming the repository.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publication identified: external_resources names two preprints with DOIs 10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and 10.1101/2024.11.03.621734; datasets shared via the public release.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: full author list of 47 names, year, title, https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C.
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete, directly usable data citation in repository-recommended form, with the DOI repeated in a machine-readable slot.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: RO_CRATE; conforms_to naming RO-Crate, ARK persistent identifiers, the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology serialized as JSON-LD and RDF-XML, and JSON-Schema dataset schemas; regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance citing the FAIR Principles as an NIH requirement.
sub_elements.quality_note: Community standards are named at packaging, identifier, provenance and schema levels, each specific enough to resolve to a specification.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: CM4AI project portal including documentation, data releases, tools and training at https://cm4ai.org/; data releases page; Cell Mapping Toolkit user documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/; FAIRSCAPE with tutorial and installation instructions at https://fairscape.github.io; page giving the Dataverse landing page.
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation, training and tooling entry points are each linked, and the portal entry states what a visitor will find there.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared condition.
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven entries with relationship_type values is_new_version_of (four prior quarterly releases), is_described_by (two preprints) and references (one Nature paper), each with target_dataset DOI and name.
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationship types are used precisely, and the references entry carries a caveat explaining that the Nature paper reports U2OS cells with the same methods and is a separate study rather than a description of this release. That distinction is exactly what a typed relation is for.

strengths: Source conflicts are resolved explicitly and by a declared ranking rule rather than silently averaged, covering the release date discrepancy between the portal and Dataverse, the AP-MS 'coming soon' contradiction, and the shift of perturb-seq links from Sequence Read Archive to embargoed.

The record declines to assert figures its sources do not support at release scope, notably the protein count for the image archives, and states the evidential reason: the June 2026 archives match the October 2025 file sizes but carry different MD5 checksums, indicating regeneration.

Funding transparency is complete and correctly formatted, with three funders, four NIH identifiers that all parse for their stated activity and institute codes, and a RePORTER cross-reference giving principal investigator, project period and award amount.

Attribution covers 47 creators with 38 ORCIDs and declared conventions for the nine without, plus ROR identifiers where the source listing printed one, with the convention documented in source_caveats rather than applied silently.

Ethics documentation is substantive without overclaiming: oversight is described as the CM4AI Ethics module with named contacts and a described methodology, and the absence of IRB approval is explained by the absence of human subjects rather than left blank.
Version lineage is fully traversable, with five releases each addressable by DOI and an explanation of why each quarterly release is a separate Dataverse dataset.
weaknesses: No variables slot and no is_tabular flag, so a reuser cannot learn from the record what fields the SEC-MS, AP-MS and perturb-seq tables contain. This costs points in both Element 3 and Element 5.

No software_and_tools slot and no software versions anywhere. The processing software that is named belongs to the MuSIC pipeline, whose outputs the record says are not in this release, and to FAIRSCAPE packaging; what processed the distributed mass spectrometry and single-cell archives is unstated.

No errata or change-log entry saying what changed at release scope relative to October 2025, even though the record demonstrably knows: regenerated image archives, newly added AP-MS archives, newly embargoed perturb-seq links.

No anomalies documentation. Outliers, batch effects, failed acquisitions and QC exclusions within the released data are not addressed; the only QC statement is that CRISPR screen data were being quality controlled at the time of the preprint.

The publisher slot is empty by deliberate choice while the record's own citation names University of Virginia Dataverse as the publishing repository, an internal tension between the record's evidence rule and its own asserted citation.
Conflicts of interest are not addressed in the ethical review documentation.
recommendations: Add a software_and_tools block naming the per-modality processing software with versions: the mass spectrometry search and quantification tools behind the AP-MS and SEC-MS archives, the alignment and demultiplexing pipeline behind the perturb-seq archives, and the FAIRSCAPE client version that packaged the release.
Add variables entries, or at minimum a data dictionary reference and an is_tabular flag, for the tabular archives in the release.
Add an errata or release-notes entry recording what changed relative to the October 2025 release, promoting the change evidence already reasoned out in source_caveats.
Populate anomalies with QC outcomes for the released archives, including any excluded acquisitions, batch structure or known artifacts, distinct from the missing-data documentation already present.
Record University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) as publisher, citing the record's own data citation as the source.
Add a conflicts-of-interest statement to ethical_reviews, or state explicitly that none were declared.
